generationMode: single built-in edit call with both required images

lightingIsotropy.method: Thirty-six full-angle luminance-gradient bins over non-water pixels; gradients below 12 were omitted.

terrainFractions.method: Native-resolution plan-area estimate: open and gently broken shelf counted as buildable; crag faces, coastal rock and cliff bands counted as steep; forest and rough non-steep ground remain in neither class.

crown.method: Full-frame dark-green local-apex census with one response per crown; horizontal skirt span measured at native resolution and converted to the 2560 px canvas, retaining saplings.

reviewNotes: The raw square edit result is preserved byte-for-byte; the source was not resized, cropped or retouched.
The northern coast water lies in the generated context margin and is included in the complete source-space water mask.
The model repainted portions of the authored context margin; the pipeline binding is expected to restore those neighbour pixels, so the stitched grey-boundary seam still requires review.
Several conifer crowns visibly retain internal light-dark modelling instead of a strictly single flat value; this is a visual contract risk, not cleared by the aggregate isotropy metric.
The beacon crag is present and bare, but its apparent flat top should be checked by the owner against the requested site scale.
Right-side stepped basalt bands are inherited or continued natural terrain; no rune marks, buildings, roads, bridges, figures or rail were added.
